items.title: OpenAI adjusts GPT-6.2 usage limits after billing error, Astra usage now counts 40% faster and Sol 25% faster [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: OpenAI corrected a billing mistake that had previously discounted GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol usage for most users, resulting in faster consumption of usage allowances. The company said users will now reach their limits 40% faster on Astra and 25% faster on Sol compared to last week, though these models still offer more usage than earlier versions. Other models were unaffected, and OpenAI will not charge users retroactively for the difference. As compensation, OpenAI is granting one banked reset to all users on Go, Plus, Pro, and Business plans.

items.title: Google requires AI agents to use Workspace MCP servers from February 2027, limiting Gmail API email sending to partners [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Google announced that starting February 1, 2027, any AI-driven tool accessing Gmail, Drive, Calendar, and other Workspace services must use its MCP servers. The new policy restricts AI agents from sending, replying, or forwarding emails via the public Gmail API, reserving these capabilities for partners with special access. Independent developers will be limited to creating drafts without the ability to modify or send them, and direct REST API calls by AI agents will face standard-tier quotas and potential policy violations. The MCP servers offer uneven API coverage, with Docs, Slides, and Tasks nearly fully supported, while Gmail and Drive have significant gaps affecting real workflows. Google also introduced data processing rules limiting Workspace data use to active, user-authorized tasks, requiring deletion upon user disconnect, and capping retention of technical information at 30 days. These changes impact developers building AI assistants with memory or long-term data indexing. Google's broad definition of AI agents includes personal scripts and third-party services, requiring self-declaration via an OAuth client checkbox. Non-compliant clients risk access restrictions or account suspension. The policy aims to control AI agent access and data usage within Workspace but raises concerns about independent developers' capabilities compared to large AI vendors with partner access.

items.title: Anthropic releases a shorter Lean 4 formal verification of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions
items.content_text: Anthropic and collaborators have produced a shorter version of a Lean 4 formal proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH) for Dirichlet L-functions, based on Levent Alpöge's work and using Mathlib. The project includes two editions: a readable version with about 300,000 lines and a compact version with about 76,000 lines, both requiring Lean v4.35.0 and Mathlib. The proof has passed machine verification but has not been reviewed by mathematicians or published as a paper, and it is licensed under Apache 2.0 by Anthropic.

items.title: The New York Times advises freelance photographers to avoid Adobe Photoshop 2027 update due to AI features that may alter metadata [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: The New York Times has instructed its freelance photographers not to update to Adobe Photoshop 2027 because the new AI-powered features can embed metadata indicating images were AI-generated or edited, which conflicts with the newspaper's policy of minimal photo manipulation. The email from Times photography leaders highlights concerns that these AI features, some of which may not be obvious to users, could undermine reader trust by suggesting photos have been digitally altered beyond acceptable standards. Adobe's 2027 Photoshop update includes an AI Assisted Editor toolbar, AI-driven editing instructions, prompt-based transformations, upscaling, and image recomposition tools. The Times' caution follows Adobe's rollout of C2PA metadata support that flags AI-generated or AI-edited content. The newspaper's spokesperson confirmed the restriction applies to Photoshop version 28.0.0 and later for assignments, though specific features causing the metadata changes have not been detailed. Adobe has not yet responded to requests for clarification.

items.title: Moat launches as a $5/month AI model access service offering wholesale pricing and unlimited usage as an alternative to OpenRouter [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Moat introduces a membership service providing access to high-quality AI models at wholesale prices for $5 per month, positioning itself as a cost-effective alternative to OpenRouter. The service offers unlimited usage with no spending caps and includes models benchmarked for full quality at discounted rates. The membership pools usage from a large user base to negotiate lower token prices, with discounts ranging from 40% to 70% on various AI models. Moat offers monthly and yearly plans, with the yearly plan billed at $60, and also supports team accounts with flexible spending limits. The service aims to pay for itself through savings on token costs for users with moderate to high usage.

items.title: Thinking Machines and Mantic develop scalable AI forecasting agent using synthetic questions and low-latency data tools to improve prediction accuracy and cost-efficiency [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Thinking Machines, in collaboration with Mantic, developed a scalable forecasting agent trained on a large pool of synthetic and real-world questions to enhance predictive accuracy and reduce costs. The agent integrates research and prediction stages, leveraging a post-training stack on the Tinker platform to handle thousands of concurrent rollouts efficiently. The team addressed data scarcity and latency challenges by generating 45,000 synthetic forecasting questions from news sources and maintaining a low-latency, point-in-time data infrastructure, including a comprehensive historical Wikipedia database. This setup enables the agent to access relevant information as it existed at the time of each forecast, significantly speeding up training compared to relying on third-party APIs. To manage the inherent noise in probabilistic forecasting, the researchers combined outcome-based rewards with expected scores from reference forecasts generated by frontier models, reducing stochasticity and biasing training toward optimal predictions. This approach contributed to the agent's competitive performance, including outperforming human forecasters in the 2026 Metaculus Cup competition.

items.title: Percona tests Sixta AI tool for MySQL troubleshooting integrated with Percona Monitoring and Management [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Percona evaluates Sixta, an AI-assisted tool designed to help diagnose and resolve MySQL database issues by integrating it with Percona Monitoring and Management (PMM). The article examines how AI can improve the efficiency and accuracy of database problem-solving. It explores the practical application of Sixta in real-world MySQL troubleshooting scenarios using PMM's monitoring capabilities.

items.title: Linus Torvalds criticizes AI-generated Linux kernel patches, urges separate testing branches and warns against introducing bugs during release candidates [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Linus Torvalds expressed strong criticism of AI-generated patches in the Linux kernel development process, emphasizing that such fixes can introduce subtle bugs. He urged developers to conduct new development and testing on separate branches and to avoid merging large updates during release candidate phases to maintain stability. Torvalds highlighted the importance of the release candidate period for identifying and resolving issues before final releases. He warned that ignoring this process and merging extensive AI-generated changes prematurely could lead to significant conflicts and instability in the kernel.

items.title: Analysis: AI adoption is gradual with significant progress in autonomous tasks but limited impact on employment data so far [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: The article argues that artificial intelligence is not overhyped, highlighting its steady progress in automating complex tasks and producing knowledge faster than experts can fully understand. Despite these advancements, widespread adoption remains limited, and AI's impact is not yet visible in employment statistics. The author describes AI's evolution as a gradual tide rather than a sudden disruption, with early signs including reduced hiring of young workers in AI-exposed jobs. The piece emphasizes that while AI is transforming work, this change unfolds over time and varies across industries and roles.

items.title: Analysis of large language models shows rapid cost declines and improved capabilities amid rising usage and stable overall expenses [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: The article examines recent developments in large language models (LLMs), highlighting significant reductions in cost per token and advances in performance benchmarks over the past few years. Despite these cost improvements, overall spending has remained steady due to increased token usage by businesses. The analysis draws on data from multiple sources including Epoch AI, Stanford's AI Index, and market expenditure indices to assess trends in pricing, capabilities, and adoption of LLMs. The piece discusses how LLMs have become synonymous with AI in public perception since ChatGPT's launch in late 2022, while emphasizing that other AI technologies operate under different economic models. It also notes that although benchmark costs have dropped dramatically, real-world savings are moderated by factors such as model selection and usage patterns. The article concludes with considerations on the future trajectory of LLM costs, capabilities, and their impact on productivity and infrastructure decisions.

items.title: Dr. Israel Alguindigue joins olmapp.ai advisory board
items.content_text: Dr. Israel Alguindigue has joined the advisory board of olmapp.ai, a technology company focused on artificial intelligence and related fields. The company is led by founder Riza Berkan, a scientist and entrepreneur with extensive experience in AI, nuclear engineering, and physics.

items.title: Suncly launches MCP Reliability Index showing 74% of company servers require login to reveal AI agent capabilities, with Cloudflare missing descriptions on 100% of inputs [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: AI verification startup Suncly released the MCP Reliability Index after auditing 432 company Model Context Protocol servers, finding that most servers, including those from Stripe, PayPal, and GitLab, require login before revealing AI agent capabilities. Among servers that responded without login, many left AI agents guessing input details, with Cloudflare's server missing descriptions on all tested inputs. The index highlights that only a few major companies like Microsoft and Anthropic provide fully described and open servers. Suncly co-founder Kasper Muutra emphasized the importance of independent, continuous verification as AI agents increasingly interact with sensitive corporate data and tools. Suncly plans a follow-up release in December to test actual tool behavior beyond static descriptions. The findings underscore growing security and operational risks from unverified AI tool behavior, suggesting that independent auditing will become essential as AI agents become more embedded in enterprise workflows.

items.title: Developer reflects on how using AI in software creation deepened his appreciation for his wife, a UX researcher [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A software developer shares how integrating AI tools into his programming process led to a greater understanding and appreciation of his wife's work in UX research and design. Their relationship, which began remotely during the pandemic, has grown stronger as he learned about the importance of user-centered design and research methods. He discusses his initial lack of knowledge about UX research and how his wife's expertise helped him realize the value of asking why users behave as they do before building software. This experience has influenced his approach to development and his personal relationship, highlighting the intersection of technology, design, and human connection.

items.title: AI pioneer discusses key risks of artificial intelligence, emphasizing ethical and safety concerns in recent video [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A leading AI researcher known as the 'Godfather of AI' outlined major risks associated with artificial intelligence in a recent video. He focused on ethical challenges, safety issues, and the importance of responsible AI development to prevent harmful outcomes as the technology progresses.

items.title: Global Electronics Association warns AI-driven shortages in basic PCB materials may surpass 2021 chip crisis, with constraints lasting through mid-2028 [ * ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: The Global Electronics Association warns that demand for printed circuit board (PCB) components, driven by artificial intelligence (AI) growth, is outpacing supply at every stage, potentially causing shortages worse than the 2021 global chip crisis. The report highlights that upstream materials like glass fabric, resin, and foil are constrained, affecting industries including automotive, medical, and defense. Price increases have been significant, with prepreg rising about 180% and E-glass fabric up 140% since late 2025, and shortages spreading from high-end AI server materials to standard-grade components. The association projects that these supply constraints will persist through at least the first half of 2027, with meaningful relief unlikely before mid-2028, potentially driving further price hikes across electronic devices that rely on PCBs.

items.title: Ask HN: Developers discuss criteria for classifying projects as low-AI or not generated by AI tools like Vibecoded [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A Hacker News thread invites developers to share their minimum criteria for determining whether a project is low-AI or not created using AI tools such as Vibecoded. Participants consider factors like the extent of AI involvement in coding, human-written tests and specs, manual code contributions, and developer review processes. The discussion explores a spectrum of AI use, questioning whether projects based on one-shot prompts, AI-generated code segments, or varying levels of human oversight should be classified differently. Contributors debate how to distinguish between AI-assisted human work and predominantly AI-generated projects, highlighting challenges in enforcing such classifications.

items.title: Dell fine-tunes open-source embedding models to improve internal semantic search for enterprise RAG, addressing failures with internal terminology using distributed training and automated tuning [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Rachel Shalom from Dell presented how her team enhanced enterprise retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) search by fine-tuning open-source embedding models to better handle Dell's internal terminology. The approach involved preparing data with hard negatives, training with distributed InfoNCE loss on H100 GPUs, automating hyperparameter tuning, and evaluating models using large language models as judges. The fine-tuning addressed failures in retrieving accurate results for queries involving Dell-specific terms like PowerScale and CloudIQ, which standard embedding models struggled to understand. This work was part of Dell's agentic search system that integrates internal sources such as GitHub, Jira, and Confluence to improve information retrieval for employees.

items.title: Capita CEO Adolfo Hernandez highlights tech transformation but leaves amid AI-driven Civil Service Pension Scheme failure and financial losses [ ! ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Capita's outgoing CEO Adolfo Hernandez emphasized the company's shift toward a technology-led, AI-enabled business model in his farewell message to staff. Despite progress in client satisfaction and partnerships with major tech firms, Hernandez's tenure is overshadowed by a failed £239m Civil Service Pension Scheme project that caused financial hardship for civil servants and raised doubts about Capita's future. The pension administration contract, awarded in 2023 with a planned transition by December 2025, faced significant delays and technical issues, leading to government intervention and public criticism. Capita's financial outlook has worsened with expected losses exceeding £90m, a plunging share price, and challenges securing new public sector contracts amid government moves to insource services. The AI failure at the core of the pension scheme project has drawn scrutiny from parliamentary committees and contributed to Capita losing other contracts, including the Royal Mail pension scheme. The company's difficulties have sparked calls from MPs to reconsider ongoing contracts, highlighting ongoing uncertainty about Capita's role in public sector service delivery.

items.title: Researchers analyze AI-assisted macOS malware that steals passwords, browser data, messages, and replaces clipboard crypto addresses [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers investigated a macOS malware sample that uses AI tools for analysis and exhibits advanced capabilities including stealing login passwords, browser cookies, saved logins, history, keychain keys, and message histories from iMessage and WhatsApp. The malware also tricks users into granting Full Disk Access, replaces cryptocurrency addresses on the clipboard, and accepts remote commands for shell execution, file transfer, and self-updating. The malware was initially encountered via a deceptive popup prompting users to run terminal commands, which then downloaded and executed obfuscated JavaScript scripts. Researchers used AI-assisted reverse engineering tools to uncover the malware's functions and noted its use of techniques discussed in recent security talks to avoid user notifications during background installation. This analysis highlights the growing complexity of AI-enhanced malware and the challenges it poses for cybersecurity defenses.

items.title: US chip export restrictions and distillation technology crackdown threaten Chinese AI model development [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: US government restrictions on chip exports and increased enforcement against distillation technologies are creating obstacles for Chinese companies and research institutions developing artificial intelligence models. These measures limit access to advanced hardware and software tools critical for AI research and deployment in China, potentially slowing progress in the sector.

items.title: Devaland AI releases Open Deal Kit with 100+ prompts and 20 agents for every stage of buying a business, emphasizing source-cited analysis [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Devaland AI has launched the Open Deal Kit, a free, open-source collection of over 100 prompts, 50 skills, 20 agents, and 4 systems designed to assist buyers through every step of acquiring a business. The kit focuses on providing fully cited, verifiable analysis to help independent sponsors and small funds compete with sellers who have professional advisors. It is built to work with Claude AI and emphasizes checking citations to avoid relying on unverified summaries. The kit includes tools like the Cited Brief System and Citation Checker to produce and audit deal briefs, ensuring all factual claims trace back to source documents. Users can copy-paste prompts directly into Claude or install the kit as Claude skills for repeated use. While the kit offers a disciplined, manual approach to deal analysis, Devaland also offers Deal OS, a product that automates citation checking at scale for managing multiple deals. Open Deal Kit is licensed under MIT and intended as an analytical aid rather than legal or investment advice. It encourages users to verify outputs against original documents and is available on GitHub for anyone to use, adapt, or integrate into their acquisition workflows.

items.title: UK Financial Conduct Authority says Meta declined joint testing of Muse AI assistant before UK launch [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: The UK's Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) criticized Meta for refusing to collaborate on joint testing of its AI personal assistant, Muse, using the FCA's sandbox prior to its UK launch. The FCA expressed concerns about potential risks to consumers from deploying the technology without sufficient regulatory oversight. The FCA's head of innovation, Colin Payne, highlighted the importance of understanding how Muse interacts with customers and handles payments, especially as several UK retailers are working with Meta to integrate Muse. Meta informed the FCA of its UK plans only recently, limiting the time available for testing. Other UK regulators, including the Competition and Markets Authority and the Information Commissioner's Office, are also monitoring Muse's rollout to ensure compliance with consumer protection and data privacy laws.

items.title: Microsoft details how state-backed hackers use ARTEX AI framework to automate cyberattacks with minimal human oversight [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.content_text: Microsoft has analyzed the ARTEX AI framework, which state-backed groups from China and North Korea, along with criminal organizations, have used since July 2026 to automate cyberattacks at machine speed. ARTEX coordinates existing security tools autonomously, enabling rapid, adaptive attacks that leave defenders only minutes to respond. The framework breaks attacker goals into subgoals, assigns tasks to specialized AI agents, and continuously updates its knowledge of target systems to carry out complex operations with minimal human intervention. Microsoft observed ARTEX-driven campaigns involving massive automated password guessing and privilege escalation, noting that conventional defenses often fail due to the framework's ability to switch tactics and evade detection. To counter these threats, Microsoft recommends active deception strategies such as honeypots, artificial delays, and fake success signals designed to mislead the AI agents into aborting attacks, alongside strict access controls and real-time isolation of compromised devices. However, the effectiveness of these defenses against adaptive AI agents remains uncertain.

items.title: Workbench launches Torno, a desktop CAD tool using Claude AI to generate and refine Python-based CAD models with live 3D feedback [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Torno is a new desktop workbench that integrates Claude, an AI coding agent, to assist users in creating CAD parts by generating Python code for CAD models. It provides a live 3D view where users can point at parts, add notes, and measure dimensions, allowing the AI to understand and refine the design iteratively with every save. The tool supports features like live builds, precise measurements on the CAD model, sketching in 3D space, and importing scans for fitting parts. Torno keeps a history of builds for comparison and review, and it exports models in various formats including STEP and STL. It runs locally without uploading data, relying on the user's own Claude instance, and is currently developed primarily for Linux and macOS environments.

items.title: 42 state attorneys general seek to block Character.AI from selling private chat histories of over 21 million users amid bankruptcy [ ! ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A bipartisan coalition of 42 state attorneys general is attempting to prevent Character.AI from selling the private chat histories of more than 21 million U.S. accounts, including over 2.1 million minors, as the company undergoes Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings. The AGs criticize the plan for lacking safeguards, such as protections for user privacy, options for data deletion, and limits on how buyers can use or resell the data. Character.AI filed for bankruptcy in October following legal challenges and controversies, including opposition to a deal where Disney acquired some assets and hired the company's CEO and technical team. The first bidder for the chat data has a limited public profile, raising further concerns. Additionally, some states have passed chatbot regulations that Character.AI may violate when they take effect in January 2027.

items.title: Memora launches self-hosted, file-first personal AI assistant with Markdown-based Second Brain and local data storage for privacy [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Memora is a self-hosted personal AI assistant designed to help users manage personal information and tasks while emphasizing privacy by keeping data locally. It integrates persistent chats, a Markdown-based Second Brain, projects, artifacts, web research, and scheduled automations into a single interface. The assistant supports streaming chat sessions, local embeddings for semantic search, and generates PDFs and other document formats without external dependencies. It runs on Debian 13 with Node.js 24 and offers features like browser notifications, Telegram delivery, and multi-language support. Memora prioritizes security by requiring HTTPS and reverse proxy configurations for public exposure and stores credentials separately from code and data.

items.title: VulnCheck develops AI-powered exploit pipeline to increase exploit production from 22 per month to over 200 per week by late 2026 [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: VulnCheck has integrated AI into its exploit development process, significantly boosting output from handcrafted exploits to an AI-driven pipeline producing over 200 exploits weekly by November 2026. The company focused on maintaining high quality and consistency, ensuring AI-generated exploits include all necessary detection artifacts such as version scanners and network rules. This shift addresses concerns about AI-driven exploit production outpacing traditional human efforts and aims to keep VulnCheck competitive in delivering timely security intelligence to its customers.

items.title: Analysis of presentation slide evolution highlights shift from text-heavy to visually engaging formats to improve audience attention
items.content_text: The article examines how presentation slides have evolved from traditional, text-dense formats to more visually appealing and engaging designs. It emphasizes the growing focus on storytelling and design elements to capture and maintain audience interest, moving away from the conventional 'boring slides' of the past.

items.title: Microsoft highlights Copilot as work OS with new agent governance and launches Azure Cobalt 200 VMs, Azure HorizonDB, and Windows Server 2028 at Ignite 2026 [ ! ] [ ⬢ ]
items.content_text: At Microsoft Ignite 2026, the company positioned Copilot as the central operating system for work, introducing enhanced agent identity, governance, and cost management features across Azure, Foundry, Entra, and Defender. Key product announcements included the general availability of Azure Cobalt 200 virtual machines with improved performance, previews of confidential computing capabilities, and new tools for deploying AI agents and models. Microsoft also unveiled Azure HorizonDB, a continuous improvement loop within Foundry, Microsoft IQ, a standalone Azure AI Gateway, and previewed the upcoming Windows Server 2028. The event emphasized transparency in AI operations, with CEO Satya Nadella announcing an AI Transparency Initiative aligned with NIST standards and rejecting opaque model auditing methods.

items.title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei says some AI deployments may need to slow to allow worker adaptation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has suggested that the rollout of certain artificial intelligence technologies might require a slower pace to give workers adequate time to adjust to the changes AI integration brings to the workplace. items.title: Researchers propose a background-independent algebraic quantization of vacuum general relativity using null cones, deriving finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces and recovering black hole entropy corrections
items.content_text: Researchers propose a background-independent quantization of vacuum general relativity on four-dimensional Lorentzian spacetimes by solving gravitational constraints on intersecting null cones and promoting canonical Poisson brackets to commutation relations. They construct a nonperturbative Hilbert space representation and obtain a Lorentzian path integral with absolutely convergent sums over intermediate states. The approach yields finite closed-form expressions for graviton pair creation and annihilation amplitudes, avoiding divergences found in perturbative expansions. Using diffeomorphism invariance, the team shows that macroscopic causal diamonds have finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces and derives the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy for marginally trapped surfaces, including logarithmic corrections for large Schwarzschild black holes consistent with previous Euclidean methods. They also derive the semiclassical Einstein equations to one loop as the low-energy limit of their theory, providing a new algebraic framework for quantum gravity.
